records.text: And the rulers and all the people said to the priests and false prophets: There is no sentence of death for this man, because he spoke to us in the name of the Lord our God.
And men from the land’s elders rose and said to the whole congregation of the people:

Micah the Morathite lived in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah and said to all Judah’s people: Thus said the Lord: Zion will be plowed as a field, Jerusalem will become an untrodden place, and the house’s mountain a grove of woodland.

Did Hezekiah and all Judah kill him? Was it not that they feared the Lord and entreated the Lord’s face, and the Lord ceased from the evils He spoke against them? And we have done great evils against our own lives!
A psalm of Asaph. The God of gods, the Lord, spoke and summoned the earth from the sun’s risings to its settings.
From Zion comes the splendor of His beauty; God will come manifestly,
our God, and He will not keep silent; fire will burn before Him, and around Him is a mighty tempest.
He will summon heaven above and the earth, to judge His people.
Gather His holy ones to Him, those who establish His covenant over sacrifices.
The heavens will announce His righteousness, for God is judge. Diapsalma.
Go, My people, enter your inner rooms, shut your door, hide for a little, a very little while, until the Lord’s wrath passes.
For behold, the Lord brings wrath from the holy place upon those dwelling on the earth. The earth will uncover its blood and will not cover those killed.
Fire will go ahead before Him and set His enemies aflame all around.
His lightning flashes shone upon the inhabited world; the earth saw and was shaken.
The mountains melted like wax before the Lord, before the Lord of all the earth.
Rub away your calf, Samaria! My anger was provoked against them. How long will they be incapable of being cleansed
in Israel? A craftsman made it, and it is no god, because your calf was leading people astray, Samaria.
The utterance against Damascus. Behold, Damascus will be removed from the cities and become a ruin,
abandoned for everlasting time, a bed and resting place for flocks, with no one pursuing.

There will no longer be a stronghold for Ephraim to flee to, nor a kingdom in Damascus, and the Syrians’ remainder will perish; for you are no better than Israel’s sons and their glory. Thus says the Lord Sabaoth.

You shall burn the graven images of their gods with fire. You shall not covet the silver or gold upon them, nor take it unto yourself, lest you stumble thereby; for it is an abomination unto the Lord your God.
And you shall not bring an abomination into your house, lest you become a thing under the ban, like unto it. You shall utterly reject it, and utterly abhor it, for it is a thing under the ban.
My belly boiled over and will not be silent; days of poverty overtook me.
I have gone about groaning without a muzzle; I have stood in an assembly, crying out.
I have become a brother to sirens and a companion to ostriches.
My skin has darkened greatly, and my bones are scorched from heat.
My lyre became an expression of my suffering, and my song became weeping for me.”
In King Hezekiah’s fourteenth year, Sennacherib king of the Assyrians went up against Judah’s fortified cities and captured them.

Hezekiah king of Judah sent messengers to the king of the Assyrians at Lachish: ‘I have sinned. Withdraw from me; whatever you impose on me, I will bear.’ The king of the Assyrians imposed on Hezekiah king of Judah three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.
Hezekiah gave all the silver found in the Lord’s house and in the treasuries of the king’s house.
At that time Hezekiah cut apart the doors of the Lord’s sanctuary and the fixed supports which Hezekiah king of Judah had gilded, and gave them to the king of the Assyrians.

The king of the Assyrians sent Tharthan, Raphis, and Rhapsakes from Lachish to King Hezekiah against Jerusalem with a great force. They went up, came to Jerusalem, and stood at the aqueduct of the upper pool, on the road of the Fuller’s Field.
David lamented this lament over Saul and over Jonathan his son,
and he gave orders to teach the sons of Judah—behold, it is written in the Book of the Upright—
“Set up a memorial, Israel, for the dead, slain upon your heights! How the mighty have fallen!
Do not report it in Gath, and do not proclaim good news in Ashkelon’s exits, lest the daughters of the foreigners rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised exult.
“On that day,” says the Lord God, “the sun will set at midday, and the light will grow dark upon the earth in daytime.

I will turn your festivals to mourning and all your songs to lamentation. I will put sackcloth on every waist and baldness on every head; I will make him like mourning for a beloved one, and those with him like a day of pain.
